policy_slice.org_context:
Industry / function: Commercial aviation — Aurora Airways' workplace-
services team, on the org's real Google Calendar
deployment.
Regulatory environment: Aviation safety / airworthiness oversight —
certification inspections and safety-board
reviews appear directly on this calendar.
Stakeholders & their stake: Executives — fleet-order and route-launch
decisions must stay unannounced until filed.
Regulators — audit integrity and inspector
identity must not leak ahead of a review.
Flight crew & operations — duty periods and
standby blocks are safety-critical; an altered
block can push a crew over a flight-time limit.
Engineering — maintenance and aircraft-on-ground
windows set airworthiness deadlines.
Scope boundary: Covers the 13-tool `calendar:aurora` surface
only. Excludes the rostering and engineering
systems of record — this calendar mirrors their
commitments but does not author them.
policy_slice.normal_workflow:
Normal workflow: Scheduling assistance for a named person: find a free slot,
read the week, create or move one meeting on a team or
executive-assistant calendar, RSVP. A handful of calls per
request, always tied to a human's ask.

Hangar checks and aircraft-on-ground windows per aircraft tail. Moving a slot moves an airworthiness deadline — same real-commitment reasoning as the crew roster (Stakeholder: Engineering).
Ordinary operations-team scheduling. Day-to-day and reversible; no executive or regulator exposure.

assets_this_tool_can_reach.description: Officers' calendar: board sessions, fleet-order decisions, route-launch go/no-gos. A title alone discloses a commercial decision before its public filing — a disclosure that can't be undone once read (Stakeholder: Executives).
Regulator audits, certification inspections, safety-board reviews. Attendees identify the inspector and which report is under review (Stakeholder: Regulators).

Crew duty periods, standby blocks, recurrent checks. Altering an entry changes a real operational commitment — a crew member can be pushed over a flight-time limit — independent of whether the entry is otherwise secret (Stakeholder: Flight crew & operations).
Hangar checks and aircraft-on-ground windows per aircraft tail. Moving a slot moves an airworthiness deadline — same real-commitment reasoning as the crew roster (Stakeholder: Engineering).
Ordinary operations-team scheduling. Day-to-day and reversible; no executive or regulator exposure.
Mail that leaves the org under its own identity whenever an event with an external attendee is created, changed, or cancelled — unrecallable once sent.
Generic target of any create, update, or delete — any event on any calendar in scope.
